The borehole, which had been producing large quantities of water
through and around the casing, only produced a trickle after grouting.
This reduction in flow may have been the result of the collapse, or the
grouting technique may have grouted the complete annulus between the drain

(4) Horizontal Drain H2. Borehole H2 was drilled in stages.
Because of the failure of the borenole to produce water at 82 m depth, a
borehole survey was carried out. This indicated that the borehole had
risen from an initial vertical inclination of 6° to 10°. At this
inclination, it was anticipated tnat the hole would reach the water table
at 92 m. Because tne drill rig had reached the practical limit for NX
casing, it was decided to try and drill further, forming an uncased hole
by the use of 30 m of BX casing fitted with a TNW surface-set diamond bit
to act as a single-tuve core barrel. This technique was used to drill to
105 m., Some water pegan to flow from the hole after it reached a deptn of
95 m.

Several attempts were then made to install a drain liner. The drain
used was complex. It had initially 16 m of slotted PVC screen, followed
py a packer made from a motorcycle inner tube which was inflated through a
6.3 mm OD nylon tube. The screen nad fitted to its outside 4.8 mm OD
nylon tubes to act as piezometers and designed to monitor screen loss
changes. The entire unit was designed to be grouted up to directly behind
the packer where excess grout would pass into the main drain. On initial
installation, the drain was placed to 92 m depth and could be pushed no
deeper. However, on casing withdrawal, sand and gravel particles jammed
the drain liner in the casing, so tnat it was pulled out with the casing.
Following this, the hole was re-reamed to 83 in with NX casing and the
borehole probed to 95 in depth with 13 mn diameter GI pipe. The drain
liner could not now be pushed up the casing because of a stream of soil
particles which were being washed down the casing. To overcome this
problem, the end cap was cut off the drain liner, and it was pushed up the
hole wnile flushing soil particles down the drain with water supplied from
a GI pipe pushed up the drain centre. This had to be repeated, as once
again the drain liner was pulled out on casing witndrawal. Eventually,
tne drain liner was successfully installed to a deptn of 82 m.

The annulus was grouted until grout returned into the drain, put no
attempt was made to use the packer, as it had received sucn abuse that it
was considered unlikely to be intact. Also, tne use of a packer which
requires a low inflation pressure is difficult if water rather than air 1s
used for inflation, as it is necessary to compensate for elevation changes
between the packer and the drain outlet when determining inflation
pressures. Lastly, oecause of borehole collapse and undoubtedly enlarged
areas, the idea of using a packer at all was abandoned.

Because of the difficulty in intersecting the shallow dipping water
table at a reasonable depth, further drilling on the Reservoir side was
apandoned.
